methods.label: Use conjugates to expose real squares
methods.sourceMethod: LIVE reference and AoPS Wiki Solution 1: introduce the real quantities z times its conjugate and z plus its conjugate, then complete two squares. The Cartesian expansion and legitimate discriminant argument in the supplied AoPS article were also checked.

annotationRationale: Conjugate products turn the modulus equation into an equality involving real quantities. Completing squares and the nonnegative zero-sum criterion force their values. Cartesian expansion, a discriminant calculation, and AM-GM equality express the same forcing step, so they are consolidated into one method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is correct; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Writing z=a+bi independently reduces the equation to (a²+b²−6)²+4(a+1)²=0. Thus z=−1±i√5 and z+6/z=−2, choice A. Both solutions are nonzero, so the requested quotient is defined. The stem, choices and key agree.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: There are no shared-bank methods. LIVE's substitution and AoPS Solution 1 are retained together. AoPS's Cartesian and legitimate discriminant calculations express the same real-square forcing and need no separate route. Answer-choice guesses do not independently establish the result and are appropriately omitted; AM-GM would repackage the same bound.
review.annotationCheck: Conjugate division, square completion and the nonnegative zero-sum criterion are appropriate assessed concepts. Modulus and complex multiplication are correctly supporting concepts.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The expansions give |z+2|²=p+2s+4 and |z²+1|²=p²+s²−2p+1. Substitution produces (p−6)²+(s+2)²=0. Since p and s are real, p=6 and s=−2; the compatible solutions are both retained. Nonzero z and 6/z=conjugate(z) then follow.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE and AoPS Solution 1 arguments match the stated basis and are correctly treated as third-party material. The candidate adds its own motivation and prerequisite explanation. It avoids the dropped negative imaginary part and unsupported answer-choice shortcuts appearing elsewhere in the AoPS article.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The target expression motivates seeking |z|²=6. Conjugation, the product identity, the substitutions and the real nonnegativity requirement are explained at use. The difficult forcing step and compatibility check are complete.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h098 supplies modulus, cnm_h102 multiplication, and cnm_h103 conjugation and quotient rationalization. The two local nodes precisely cover square completion and the inference from a zero sum of nonnegative real terms.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three complex-number nodes match their native topics, with only the modulus component of the geometric-meaning node used. No accepted CN links are supplied for the two local algebraic principles.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: N-CN.A.2 and N-CN.A.3 support multiplication and conjugate-based modulus/division. A-SSE.B.3b supports the square-completion manipulation, without function-extremum interpretation. N-CN.C.8 has partial identity overlap; complex-plane representation, polar form, distance and midpoint links are not exercised.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All five nodes match explicit steps. The explanation correctly applies the zero-sum criterion to real p and s, rather than to arbitrary complex squares.
